title: CREATE VIEW
description: Learn how to create views using the CREATE VIEW statement.

data.text: To create a new view in SQL Server, use the CREATE VIEW statement. The view is defined by a SELECT statement that can refer to one or more tables.

data.title: Basic CREATE VIEW syntax
data.content: Creates a view from a SELECT statement.

data.title: Create a daily sales view
data.content: Creates a view that summarizes daily sales.
data.code:
CREATE VIEW sales.daily_sales
AS
SELECT
    year(order_date) AS y,
    month(order_date) AS m,
    day(order_date) AS d,
    p.product_id,
    product_name,
    quantity * i.list_price AS sales
FROM
    sales.orders AS o
INNER JOIN sales.order_items AS i
    ON o.order_id = i.order_id
INNER JOIN production.products AS p
    ON p.product_id = i.product_id;

data.text: Once the view is created, you can query it like a table:

data.title: Query the view
data.content: Selects all data from the daily_sales view.
data.code:
SELECT * FROM sales.daily_sales
ORDER BY y, m, d, product_name;

data.text: Use CREATE VIEW OR ALTER to modify an existing view:

data.title: OR ALTER to add columns
data.content: Redefines the view with additional columns.
data.code:
CREATE OR ALTER sales.daily_sales (
    year,
    month,
    day,
    customer_name,
    product_id,
    product_name,
    sales
)
AS
SELECT
    year(order_date),
    month(order_date),
    day(order_date),
    concat(first_name, ' ', last_name),
    p.product_id,
    product_name,
    quantity * i.list_price
FROM
    sales.orders AS o
    INNER JOIN sales.order_items AS i
        ON o.order_id = i.order_id
    INNER JOIN production.products AS p
        ON p.product_id = i.product_id
    INNER JOIN sales.customers AS c
        ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id;

data.title: CREATE VIEW Key Points
points: CREATE VIEW saves a SELECT query as a named object in the database.
Use OR ALTER to modify an existing view without dropping it.
Views do not store data — they execute the underlying query each time.
You can explicitly define a column list or derive it from the SELECT statement.
